question.problem:
For the functions $u(x)$ and $v(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
u(4)=1,\,{u}^{′}(4)=6,\,v(4)=-2,\,{v}^{′}(4)=2
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}u(x)+3v(x))$ at $x=4.$

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}u(x)+3v(x))|}_{x=4}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}u(x)+3v(x))=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{′}(x)+3{v}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=4$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}u(x)+3v(x))|}_{x=4} & =\frac{1}{2}{u}^{′}(4)+3{v}^{′}(4) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(6)+3(2) \\  & =3+6 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
